- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for downward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns negative.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; re-estimate from midpoint of sentiment transition.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 2–5% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “-0.33” entries, model underperforms; add 1–2% to forecast to compensate for suppressed sentiment.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >5% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent trend unless sentiment strongly contradicts.
